html:
Most ordinary text just gets rendered as is: punctuation (3 < 4 & "quotes"), letters of any script (naïve, 日本語), and emoji 🎉 👍 🇺🇸, untouched. There are no :smile: shortcodes.

  • bold and bold
  • italic and italic
  • both
  • code, and a ` in code
  • a link (a new tab) and a local one
  • bare: https://example.com, www.example.com, me@example.com
  • a message: MSG_plans_3
  • not markup: snake_case_name, a * lone star, 2 * 3
  • struck, ~5 minutes, and *escaped* stars

html:
A fence keeps its text exactly, markup and all:

const s = "**not bold**";

tildes fence too, here with no language

A longer fence holds a shorter one, which stays text:

```zig
const x = 1;
```

The chat's quote fence shows a message as written, its own fences included:

Here is my fix:
```zig
const y = 2;
```
